## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

questions.question: How should the /admin product manager be protected? It performs live create/edit/delete on your catalog.

options.label: Password gate
options.description: One shared admin password stored in an env var; a login page sets a secure cookie; middleware guards /admin and the admin APIs. Fast, no new dependencies, good for a small team. (Recommended)

options.label: Supabase Auth
options.description: Per-user email/password accounts via Supabase Auth. More robust and multi-user, but more setup (user table, invite flow).

options.label: No login
options.description: Anyone with the /admin URL can edit. Easiest, but unsafe for a live catalog. Not recommended.

## Context

OSIMIRI's product catalog is currently **static** — defined in `lib/product-demo.ts` (`demoProducts`, ~50-field `DemoProduct` shape) and rendered by `app/products/page.tsx` and `app/products/[slug]/page.tsx`. Adding or editing a product means a code change and redeploy.

The client wants a **self-serve admin tool** to manage the live catalog: create, edit, delete, **bulk import (CSV)**, multi-select bulk actions, and **image uploads** — styled after the Shopify Products admin (grounded via refero screen `7a111fa7`: left nav, "Products" title, Export/Import/Add buttons, tabbed table with checkbox bulk-select + bulk action bar, status badges, thumbnails).

**Outcome:** A protected `/admin` area where the team manages products in Supabase; the public `/products` pages read live from that data.

### Confirmed decisions
- **Auth:** Password gate (shared env password → signed cookie → middleware).
- **Site wiring:** Replace static catalog — public product pages read live from Supabase; seed table from `demoProducts` so nothing is lost.
- **Backend:** Supabase (user has a project ready) — new `products` table + Storage bucket for images.
- **Bulk:** CSV import + multi-select bulk actions.

## Architecture overview

```
/admin/login            password form  → POST /api/admin/auth (set cookie)
/admin/products         list (Shopify-style table, tabs, search, bulk bar)
/admin/products/new     create form (sectioned, image upload, CSV import entry)
/admin/products/[id]    edit form (same component)
middleware.ts           guards /admin/* and /api/admin/* (except login/auth)

/api/admin/products            GET(list) · POST(create)
/api/admin/products/[id]       GET · PATCH(update) · DELETE
/api/admin/products/bulk       POST (bulk delete / set-status / CSV upsert)
/api/admin/upload              POST (multipart → Supabase Storage → public URL)
/api/admin/auth                POST(login) · DELETE(logout)

lib/products.ts         server reads (getAllProducts/getProductBySlug) + DB↔Product mappers, falls back to demoProducts when Supabase unconfigured
lib/product-schema.ts   zod schema for a product (mirrors DemoProduct), reused by API + form
```

Reuses existing patterns: `createSupabaseServerClient()` / `isSupabaseConfigured()` in `lib/supabase.ts` (service-role server client), the zod-validated route pattern from `app/api/forms/[table]/route.ts`, `slugify()` in `lib/utils.ts`, and the `DemoProduct` field set as the canonical product shape.

## 1. Data layer (Supabase)

New migration `supabase/products.sql` (user runs in Supabase SQL editor):

- **Table `products`** — one column per `DemoProduct` field. Scalars as `text`/`boolean`; arrays (`galleryImageLinks`, `finishOptions`, `*Tags`, `seoKeywords`, etc.) as `text[]`; plus `id uuid pk default gen_random_uuid()`, `product_id text unique` (the human SKU like `OSI-SOF-001`), `slug text unique`, `status text default 'Draft'`, `created_at`/`updated_at timestamptz`. `updated_at` auto-bumped by a trigger.
- **RLS:** enable; **no anon policies** (so the public anon key cannot read drafts or write). All reads/writes go through server routes using the **service-role key**, which bypasses RLS. Public product pages run server-side with the service client and filter `status = 'Active'`.
- **Storage bucket `product-images`** (public read) — created via SQL/dashboard; uploads via service role.
- **Seed:** `INSERT` the 2 existing `demoProducts` so the table is non-empty and the public pages keep working immediately.

## 2. Auth — password gate

- Env: `ADMIN_PASSWORD` (the shared secret) and `ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET` (HMAC signing key).
- `app/admin/login/page.tsx`: minimal client form → `POST /api/admin/auth`.
- `app/api/admin/auth/route.ts`: timing-safe compare against `ADMIN_PASSWORD`; on success set httpOnly, secure, sameSite=lax cookie `osimiri_admin` = `payload.HMAC-SHA256(payload)` (Web Crypto, edge-safe). `DELETE` clears it.
- `middleware.ts` (matcher `['/admin/:path*','/api/admin/:path*']`): allow `/admin/login` + `/api/admin/auth`; otherwise verify cookie HMAC via Web Crypto → redirect to `/admin/login` (pages) or `401` (APIs).

## 3. Admin UI (Shopify-style, themed to OSIMIRI tokens)

Admin gets its **own shell** (no marketing Navbar/Footer):
- Add `components/layout/SiteFrame.tsx` (`"use client"`, uses `usePathname`): when path starts with `/admin`, render only `{children}`; else render the current chrome (Navbar/Footer/EnquiryModal/WhatsApp/CustomCursor). Update `app/layout.tsx` to wrap children in `SiteFrame`. (Footer is currently a server component — rendering it inside a client wrapper is fine; it has no server-only deps.)
- `app/admin/layout.tsx`: left sidebar (Products, + room to grow) + top bar (search, "Logout"), light neutral admin theme using existing `--color-*` tokens.

**Products list** `app/admin/products/page.tsx` (server fetch) + `ProductsTable` client component:
- Title "Products" + right-aligned **Import (CSV)** / **Export** / **Add product**.
- Tabs: All / Active / Draft / Archived (filter by `status`). Search box (title/SKU/category).
- Table rows: checkbox, thumbnail (`mainImageLink`), title+subtitle, status badge, collection, category, featured star.
- Selecting rows reveals a **bulk action bar** ("N selected · Set Active · Set Draft · Delete") → `POST /api/admin/products/bulk`.
- Empty state when no products.

**Create/Edit form** `app/admin/products/_components/ProductForm.tsx` (react-hook-form + zod via `@hookform/resolvers`, already deps):
- Shopify-like two-column: main column (Title, slug auto from title, descriptions, media uploader, materials/finishes, dimensions, SEO) + side column (Status, Featured, collection/category, pricing note, tags). Advanced/optional fields in collapsible sections.
- **Media uploader**: drag/drop or pick → `POST /api/admin/upload` per file → returns public URL → appended to `mainImageLink` / `galleryImageLinks` / `lifestyleImageLinks` etc. with reorder + remove.
- Submit → `POST` (create) or `PATCH` (edit). Delete button (with confirm) on edit.

**CSV import** `app/admin/products/import/page.tsx`: upload CSV → preview parsed rows → `POST /api/admin/products/bulk` upserts by `product_id`/`slug`. Provide a downloadable template (header = product fields). Parse CSV with a tiny inline parser (no new dep) or `papaparse` if approved.

## 4. API routes (service-role, zod-validated)

Mirror `app/api/forms/[table]/route.ts`: parse JSON → `productSchema.safeParse` → `createSupabaseServerClient()` insert/update/delete → typed JSON responses; `isSupabaseConfigured()` guard returns a clear "configure Supabase" message in mock mode. Map camelCase ↔ snake_case columns in `lib/products.ts`.

## 5. Public site rewiring

- `lib/products.ts`: `getAllProducts()` / `getProductBySlug()` query Supabase (`status='Active'`), map rows → `Product` (same shape as `DemoProduct`); **fall back to `demoProducts`** when `!isSupabaseConfigured()`.
- `app/products/page.tsx` → async server, list from `getAllProducts()`.
- `app/products/[slug]/page.tsx` → async server via `getProductBySlug()`; replace static `generateStaticParams` with `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` (or `revalidate`). Keep `lib/product-demo.ts` as seed + fallback (do not delete).
- Collections pages stay static (separate dataset); products relate via `collectionName`/`category`.

## Files

**Create:** `supabase/products.sql`, `lib/product-schema.ts`, `lib/products.ts`, `middleware.ts`, `components/layout/SiteFrame.tsx`, `app/admin/layout.tsx`, `app/admin/login/page.tsx`, `app/admin/products/page.tsx`, `app/admin/products/new/page.tsx`, `app/admin/products/[id]/page.tsx`, `app/admin/products/import/page.tsx`, `app/admin/products/_components/ProductsTable.tsx`, `app/admin/products/_components/ProductForm.tsx`, `app/admin/products/_components/MediaUploader.tsx`, `app/api/admin/auth/route.ts`, `app/api/admin/upload/route.ts`, `app/api/admin/products/route.ts`, `app/api/admin/products/[id]/route.ts`, `app/api/admin/products/bulk/route.ts`.

**Modify:** `app/layout.tsx` (SiteFrame), `app/products/page.tsx` + `app/products/[slug]/page.tsx` (read from `lib/products.ts`), `.env.local` keys documented in `README.md`.

## User setup (one-time, I'll provide exact values)
1. Run `supabase/products.sql` in the Supabase SQL editor.
2. Create public Storage bucket `product-images`.
3. Add to `.env.local`: `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET` (+ same in Vercel env).

## Verification
- `npm run dev`; with `.env.local` set, visit `/admin` → redirected to `/admin/login`; wrong password rejected, correct password lands on `/admin/products`.
- Create a product (with image upload) → appears in list → visible on public `/products` and `/products/<slug>`.
- Edit → change reflects on site. Delete (single + bulk) removes it.
- CSV import a 2-row file → both products created; bulk-select → Set Draft → they drop off the public list.
- Verify via preview tools: `preview_start`, snapshot `/admin/products`, screenshot the table + form; confirm no marketing Navbar/Footer on `/admin`; confirm `/products` reflects DB.
- Confirm `middleware` blocks `/api/admin/products` without the cookie (401).

import { z } from "zod";
import type { DemoProduct } from "@/lib/product-demo";

/**
 * The canonical product shape used across the app is the same rich shape as the
 * original static catalogue (`DemoProduct`). Managed products read from Supabase
 * are mapped into this exact type so every existing page keeps working.
 */
export type Product = DemoProduct & { id?: string };

export const PRODUCT_STATUSES = ["Active", "Draft", "Archived"] as const;
export type ProductStatus = (typeof PRODUCT_STATUSES)[number];

const optionalText = z
  .string()
  .trim()
  .optional()
  .transform((v) => (v === "" ? undefined : v));

const stringArray = z
  .array(z.string().trim().min(1))
  .optional()
  .default([]);

/**
 * Validation for create/update payloads coming from the admin form or CSV.
 * Only `title` is strictly required — everything else has a sensible default so
 * a product can be saved as a draft early and completed later (Shopify-style).
 */
export const productInputSchema = z.object({
  productId: optionalText,
  title: z.string().trim().min(2, "Title is required."),
  subtitle: optionalText,
  slug: optionalText,
  collectionName: z.string().trim().default(""),
  category: z.string().trim().default(""),
  subCategory: optionalText,
  status: z.enum(PRODUCT_STATUSES).default("Draft"),
  featuredProduct: z.boolean().default(false),

  shortDescription: z.string().trim().default(""),
  fullDescription: z.string().trim().default(""),
  customizationNote: z.string().trim().default(""),
  careInstructions: optionalText,
  installationNote: optionalText,

  seoTitle: optionalText,
  seoDescription: optionalText,
  seoKeywords: stringArray,
  focusKeyword: optionalText,
  altTextMainImage: z.string().trim().default(""),

  primaryMaterial: z.string().trim().default(""),
  secondaryMaterials: stringArray,
  finishOptions: stringArray,

create table if not exists products (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  product_id text unique,
  title text not null,
  subtitle text,
  slug text unique not null,
  collection_name text default '',
  category text default '',
  sub_category text,
  status text not null default 'Draft',

  short_description text default '',
  full_description text default '',

);

## Product Manager (Admin)

A Shopify-style product manager lives at **`/admin`** (CRUD, bulk CSV import,
multi-select bulk actions, image uploads). It is backed by Supabase.

### One-time setup

1. **Database & storage** — open the Supabase SQL editor and run
   [`supabase/products.sql`](supabase/products.sql). It creates the `products`
   table (RLS on, no anon policies), a public `product-images` Storage bucket,
   and seeds one demo product.
2. **Environment** — add these to `.env.local` (and to your Vercel project env):

   ```bash
   NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://YOUR-PROJECT.supabase.co
   SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=your-service-role-key   # server-only, keep secret
   ADMIN_PASSWORD=choose-a-strong-password           # the admin login password
   ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET=long-random-string           # signs the session cookie
   ```

3. Restart `npm run dev`, visit `/admin`, and sign in with `ADMIN_PASSWORD`.

### How it connects

- The public `/products` and `/products/[slug]` pages read **Active** products
  live from Supabase. When Supabase isn't configured, they fall back to the
  static sample in `lib/product-demo.ts`, so the site always renders.
- All admin reads/writes go through `/api/admin/*` routes using the service-role
  key. `middleware.ts` guards `/admin` and `/api/admin` behind the session
  cookie.

All six tasks complete and committed (`ed0a052`, 28 files). Here's the wrap-up.

## What you got — a Shopify-style Product Manager at `/admin`

**Built & verified working:**
- **Auth** — password gate. `/admin` redirects to a login page; wrong password rejected (401), correct one sets a signed cookie. `proxy.ts` guards every `/admin` page and `/api/admin` route (verified: 307 redirect / 401 without a session, 200 with).
- **Products list** — Shopify-style table: All/Active/Draft/Archived tabs, search, thumbnails, status badges, featured star, and a **multi-select bulk bar** (Set Active/Draft/Archive/Delete). Export to CSV.
- **Create/Edit form** — every field from your product model, grouped (details, media, materials/dimensions, collapsible SEO & logistics), with **drag-and-drop image upload** for main/gallery/lifestyle/detail/swatch images, auto-slug, and delete.
- **CSV import** — upload to bulk create/update (matched by slug), with a downloadable template and a preview before importing.
- **Site wiring** — public `/products` and `/products/[slug]` now read live from the catalogue, with automatic fallback to the static sample so the site never breaks. Admin runs in its own shell — **verified the marketing navbar/footer are hidden on `/admin`** but present on the public site.
- **Production build passes**, TypeScript clean, no deprecation warnings.

input.content:
# Plan: OSIMIRI Catalog Manager + Site per "Complete prototype for builder"

## Context

The client (UR Infra / OSIMIRI) provided a design package at
`website1/Complete prototype for builder/` — a proposal PDF (11 modules) plus a
polished **"Catalog Manager"** admin prototype (`Manage Products.dc.html`,
`screenshots/dash.png|products.png|products2.png`). It defines a far richer admin
than the CRUD tool already built, and calls for a public website redesign with
category-driven product browsing.

We already have a working password-gated `/admin` (products CRUD, image upload,
CSV, bulk) backed by Supabase (`products` table). This effort **upgrades that to
match the prototype** and adds the missing modules, then wires/redesigns the
public catalog.

**Work only in `/Users/feniljikadara/Documents/website1`** (the Vercel-connected repo).

### Confirmed decisions
- **Scope:** Everything — full admin Catalog Manager + public wiring + public redesign.
- **Prices:** Store & manage numeric ₹ in admin; **public shows "Price on request"** (no numbers).
- **Modules:** All — Overview dashboard, Categories & subcategories, Media Library, Activity Log (plus existing Products CRUD + SEO, restyled).

### Design system (from the prototype)
- Green `#2f6b4e` (primary / sidebar / buttons), dark `#285a42`; light-green accent `#e8f1ec`.
- Warm neutrals: `#faf9f6` bg, `#f1ede6`, `#e7e3db`/`#ddd9d1` borders, text `#4a463f`/`#56514a`/`#8a857c`.
- Danger `#b4493d`, gold `#b08d57`.
- Fonts: **IBM Plex Sans** (UI) + **IBM Plex Mono** (SKU, prices, counts).

## Realistic phasing (ship in this order)
This is a multi-module build. Execute and verify phase-by-phase; each phase is independently useful.

### Phase 1 — Admin design system + shell
- Add IBM Plex Sans/Mono via `next/font/google`, scoped to admin.
- Admin theme tokens as CSS vars scoped under the admin layout wrapper (`[data-admin]`) in `app/globals.css` (keep the site's gold/brown theme untouched).
- Rebuild `app/admin/(panel)/layout.tsx` sidebar to match prototype: brand "O · OSIMIRI / Catalog Manager"; nav **Overview / Products / Categories / Media Library / Activity Log** with count badges; footer "Live site — osimiri.in · synced" + user (`Himanshu Jain / Admin`) with logout.

### Phase 2 — Data layer (new migration `supabase/catalog.sql`)
- **`categories`**: `id, name, slug, parent_id (self-FK for subcategory), position, created_at`. Seed the prototype's 6 categories + subcategories (Living Room→Sofas/Armchairs/Coffee Tables, Bedroom→Beds/Nightstands, Dining→Dining Tables/Chairs, Office, Outdoor, Lighting).
- **`activity_log`**: `id, action ('created'|'updated'|'deleted'|'published'|'uploaded'), entity, entity_id, title, created_at`.
- **`products`** additions: `price numeric` (nullable), `category_id uuid` FK (leaf category). Keep existing `product_id` as SKU and legacy `collection_name`/`category` text for back-compat/fallback.
- Reseed the prototype's 12 products (names, SKUs `OSM-LR-1042`, ₹ prices, categories, statuses Published/Draft) so the UI matches the mockups. Extend `lib/product-schema.ts` (add `price`, `categoryId`) + `PRODUCT_FIELD_MAP`.
- Media Library reads the existing Storage bucket `product-images` (no new table needed) via `supabase.storage.from(...).list()`.

### Phase 3 — Admin modules (restyle + new), reusing existing API pattern

```
/admin/products         list (Shopify-style table, tabs, search, bulk bar)

/admin/products/[id]    edit form (same component)
middleware.ts           guards /admin/* and /api/admin/* (except login/auth)

/api/admin/products            GET(list) · POST(create)
/api/admin/products/[id]       GET · PATCH(update) · DELETE
/api/admin/products/bulk       POST (bulk delete / set-status / CSV upsert)
/api/admin/upload              POST (multipart → Supabase Storage → public URL)
/api/admin/auth                POST(login) · DELETE(logout)

lib/products.ts         server reads (getAllProducts/getProductBySlug) + DB↔Product mappers, falls back to demoProducts when Supabase unconfigured
lib/product-schema.ts   zod schema for a product (mirrors DemoProduct), reused by API + form
```

- **RLS:** enable; **no anon policies** (so the public anon key cannot read drafts or write). All reads/writes go through server routes using the **service-role key**, which bypasses RLS. Public product pages run server-side with the service client and filter `status = 'Active'`.
- **Storage bucket `product-images`** (public read) — created via SQL/dashboard; uploads via service role.
- **Seed:** `INSERT` the 2 existing `demoProducts` so the table is non-empty and the public pages keep working immediately.

## 2. Auth — password gate

- Env: `ADMIN_PASSWORD` (the shared secret) and `ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET` (HMAC signing key).
- `app/admin/login/page.tsx`: minimal client form → `POST /api/admin/auth`.
- `app/api/admin/auth/route.ts`: timing-safe compare against `ADMIN_PASSWORD`; on success set httpOnly, secure, sameSite=lax cookie `osimiri_admin` = `payload.HMAC-SHA256(payload)` (Web Crypto, edge-safe). `DELETE` clears it.

# Plan: OSIMIRI Catalog Manager + Site per "Complete prototype for builder"

## Context

The client (UR Infra / OSIMIRI) provided a design package at
`website1/Complete prototype for builder/` — a proposal PDF (11 modules) plus a
polished **"Catalog Manager"** admin prototype (`Manage Products.dc.html`,
`screenshots/dash.png|products.png|products2.png`). It defines a far richer admin
than the CRUD tool already built, and calls for a public website redesign with
category-driven product browsing.

We already have a working password-gated `/admin` (products CRUD, image upload,
CSV, bulk) backed by Supabase (`products` table). This effort **upgrades that to
match the prototype** and adds the missing modules, then wires/redesigns the
public catalog.

**Work only in `/Users/feniljikadara/Documents/website1`** (the Vercel-connected repo).

### Confirmed decisions
- **Scope:** Everything — full admin Catalog Manager + public wiring + public redesign.
- **Prices:** Store & manage numeric ₹ in admin; **public shows "Price on request"** (no numbers).
- **Modules:** All — Overview dashboard, Categories & subcategories, Media Library, Activity Log (plus existing Products CRUD + SEO, restyled).

### Design system (from the prototype)
- Green `#2f6b4e` (primary / sidebar / buttons), dark `#285a42`; light-green accent `#e8f1ec`.
- Warm neutrals: `#faf9f6` bg, `#f1ede6`, `#e7e3db`/`#ddd9d1` borders, text `#4a463f`/`#56514a`/`#8a857c`.
- Danger `#b4493d`, gold `#b08d57`.
- Fonts: **IBM Plex Sans** (UI) + **IBM Plex Mono** (SKU, prices, counts).

## Realistic phasing (ship in this order)
This is a multi-module build. Execute and verify phase-by-phase; each phase is independently useful.

### Phase 1 — Admin design system + shell
- Add IBM Plex Sans/Mono via `next/font/google`, scoped to admin.
- Admin theme tokens as CSS vars scoped under the admin layout wrapper (`[data-admin]`) in `app/globals.css` (keep the site's gold/brown theme untouched).
- Rebuild `app/admin/(panel)/layout.tsx` sidebar to match prototype: brand "O · OSIMIRI / Catalog Manager"; nav **Overview / Products / Categories / Media Library / Activity Log** with count badges; footer "Live site — osimiri.in · synced" + user (`Himanshu Jain / Admin`) with logout.

### Phase 2 — Data layer (new migration `supabase/catalog.sql`)
- **`categories`**: `id, name, slug, parent_id (self-FK for subcategory), position, created_at`. Seed the prototype's 6 categories + subcategories (Living Room→Sofas/Armchairs/Coffee Tables, Bedroom→Beds/Nightstands, Dining→Dining Tables/Chairs, Office, Outdoor, Lighting).
- **`activity_log`**: `id, action ('created'|'updated'|'deleted'|'published'|'uploaded'), entity, entity_id, title, created_at`.
- **`products`** additions: `price numeric` (nullable), `category_id uuid` FK (leaf category). Keep existing `product_id` as SKU and legacy `collection_name`/`category` text for back-compat/fallback.
- Reseed the prototype's 12 products (names, SKUs `OSM-LR-1042`, ₹ prices, categories, statuses Published/Draft) so the UI matches the mockups. Extend `lib/product-schema.ts` (add `price`, `categoryId`) + `PRODUCT_FIELD_MAP`.
- Media Library reads the existing Storage bucket `product-images` (no new table needed) via `supabase.storage.from(...).list()`.

### Phase 3 — Admin modules (restyle + new), reusing existing API pattern
- **Products list** (`_components/ProductsTable.tsx`): columns PRODUCT (thumb+name+SKU mono) · CATEGORY (parent/sub) · PRICE (₹ mono) · STATUS (Published/Draft pills) · IMAGES (count) · updated "2h ago"; category & status filter selects; keep bulk bar + CSV/export.
- **Product form** (`ProductForm.tsx`): add Price (₹) and Category/Subcategory selects; restyle to green theme; keep image uploader, SEO, attributes (attributes already exist as tag arrays — add a key/value "specifications" section).
- **Overview** `app/admin/(panel)/page.tsx` → dashboard: 4 stat cards (total / published / drafts / media), "Products by category" bar chart (plain CSS bars), "Recent activity" from `activity_log`.
- **Categories** `app/admin/(panel)/categories/`: list with counts, create/edit/delete, subcategory nesting → `/api/admin/categories` (GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE).
- **Media Library** `app/admin/(panel)/media/`: grid of Storage objects, upload, copy URL, delete → `/api/admin/media` (GET list, DELETE) reusing `/api/admin/upload`.
- **Activity Log** `app/admin/(panel)/activity/`: full log list.
- **Logging:** add a `logActivity()` helper in `lib/activity.ts`; call it from product create/update/delete and upload routes.

### Phase 4 — Public catalog wiring + redesign
- `lib/products.ts`: join category; **never expose numeric price** to public mappers (only `priceNote`).
- `/products`: category/subcategory browsing (filter or grouped sections) reading `categories` + Active products; product detail shows "Price on request".
- Public visual redesign: apply refreshed structure to listing/detail + key marketing pages using existing site tokens. (No public mockups were provided — this phase is iterative and will be reviewed screen-by-screen with the user; the admin phases are the mockup-backed priority.)

## Files
**New:** `supabase/catalog.sql`, `lib/activity.ts`, `app/admin/(panel)/page.tsx` (Overview), `app/admin/(panel)/categories/{page,_components}`, `app/admin/(panel)/media/page.tsx`, `app/admin/(panel)/activity/page.tsx`, `app/api/admin/categories/{route,[id]}/route.ts`, `app/api/admin/media/route.ts`, `app/api/admin/activity/route.ts`, admin dashboard components under `app/admin/_components/`.

**Modify:** `app/admin/(panel)/layout.tsx`, `app/admin/_components/{ProductsTable,ProductForm}.tsx`, `lib/products.ts`, `lib/product-schema.ts`, `lib/product-csv.ts`, `app/globals.css` (scoped admin tokens + IBM Plex), API write routes (add `logActivity`), `app/products/page.tsx` + `app/products/[slug]/page.tsx`.

Reuse: existing service-role pattern (`lib/supabase.ts` `createSupabaseServerClient`/`isSupabaseConfigured`/`SUPABASE_SETUP_MESSAGE`/`isSupabaseSetupError`), zod route pattern, `slugify` (`lib/utils.ts`), `proxy.ts` auth guard, `MediaUploader.tsx`.

## User setup (one-time)
Run `supabase/catalog.sql` in the Supabase SQL editor (adds tables/columns + reseed). Env is already configured.

## Verification
- `npm run dev` in website1 (preview MCP is bound to the other clone, so verify via `npm run dev` + curl, and screenshots through a browser tool when available).
- Admin: login → Overview shows correct stats/chart/activity; Products list matches mockup columns (SKU, ₹, category, images); create a product with price+category → appears in list, logs an activity, shows on public site with "Price on request"; Categories CRUD; Media Library lists/uploads; Activity Log records events.
- Public: `/products` browses by category; detail page shows no numeric price.
- `npm run build` passes; commit per phase in website1 (push via GitHub Desktop).

import { z } from "zod";
import type { DemoProduct } from "@/lib/product-demo";

/**
 * The canonical product shape used across the app is the same rich shape as the
 * original static catalogue (`DemoProduct`). Managed products read from Supabase
 * are mapped into this exact type so every existing page keeps working.
 */
export type Product = DemoProduct & { id?: string };

export const PRODUCT_STATUSES = ["Active", "Draft", "Archived"] as const;
export type ProductStatus = (typeof PRODUCT_STATUSES)[number];

const optionalText = z
  .string()
  .trim()
  .optional()
  .transform((v) => (v === "" ? undefined : v));

const stringArray = z
  .array(z.string().trim().min(1))
  .optional()
  .default([]);

/**
 * Validation for create/update payloads coming from the admin form or CSV.
 * Only `title` is strictly required — everything else has a sensible default so
 * a product can be saved as a draft early and completed later (Shopify-style).
 */
export const productInputSchema = z.object({
  productId: optionalText,
  title: z.string().trim().min(2, "Title is required."),
  subtitle: optionalText,
  slug: optionalText,
  collectionName: z.string().trim().default(""),
  category: z.string().trim().default(""),
  subCategory: optionalText,
  status: z.enum(PRODUCT_STATUSES).default("Draft"),
  featuredProduct: z.boolean().default(false),

  shortDescription: z.string().trim().default(""),
  fullDescription: z.string().trim().default(""),
  customizationNote: z.string().trim().default(""),
  careInstructions: optionalText,
  installationNote: optionalText,

  seoTitle: optionalText,
  seoDescription: optionalText,
  seoKeywords: stringArray,
  focusKeyword: optionalText,
  altTextMainImage: z.string().trim().default(""),

  primaryMaterial: z.string().trim().default(""),
  secondaryMaterials: stringArray,
  finishOptions: stringArray,
  upholsteryOptions: stringArray,
  swatchReferenceCodes: stringArray,

  dimensionsOverall: z.string().trim().default(""),
  dimensionsSeatHeight: optionalText,
  dimensionsSeatDepth: optionalText,
  dimensionsCustomizable: z.boolean().default(false),
  weight: optionalText,
  assemblyRequired: z.boolean().optional(),
  leadTime: optionalText,
  warranty: optionalText,

  priceVisible: z.boolean().optional(),
  priceNote: optionalText,
  projectSuitability: stringArray,
  availabilityRegion: optionalText,

  mainImageLink: z.string().trim().default(""),
  galleryImageLinks: stringArray,
  lifestyleImageLinks: stringArray,

create extension if not exists pgcrypto;

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Categories (self-referencing for subcategories)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
create table if not exists categories (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  name text not null,
  slug text unique not null,
  parent_id uuid references categories(id) on delete cascade,
  position int not null default 0,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index if not exists categories_parent_idx on categories (parent_id);
alter table categories enable row level security;

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Activity log
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
create table if not exists activity_log (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  action text not null,           -- created | updated | deleted | published | uploaded
  entity text not null default 'product',
  entity_id text,
  title text not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index if not exists activity_log_created_idx on activity_log (created_at desc);
alter table activity_log enable row level security;

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Product additions
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
alter table products add column if not exists price numeric;
alter table products add column if not exists category_id uuid references categories(id) on delete set null;
create index if not exists products_category_idx on products (category_id);

content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme: `prefers-color-scheme` carries the OS preference, and the viewer's toggle stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, which must override the media query in both directions. The robust pattern is token-level: define the palette as custom properties on `:root`, redefine only the tokens under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — style components through the tokens, never directly inside the media query — then redefine them again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]` and `:root[data-theme="light"]`. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

Enable **MFA** on Supabase/Vercel/GitHub · confirm **Supabase backups** + do one test restore · add **error/uptime monitoring** · separate **staging DB** from prod · add real **Privacy/Terms** pages · decide whether to **purge the PDFs from git history** (they're in the pushed history).

## 🟠 Outstanding work (scope, if you want it)
No automated tests yet, and a cross-browser/device pass before sign-off.

Two notes: the fix commit is **local** (push via GitHub Desktop), and the admin "Catalog Manager" rebuild from earlier is still **half-finished** (new sidebar + Overview landed, but the Products restyle/Categories/Media/Activity pages were interrupted by the folder-lock and by the `catalog.sql` migration not being run yet). message.content:
I logged into the OSIMIRI admin portal and tested the login flow along with every section: Overview, Products (list, detail/edit, new product form), Categories, Media Library, and Activity Log, plus a quick check of mobile responsiveness. Here is a detailed breakdown of what needs attention before this can be called production grade.
Login page. The password field and layout are clean and on-brand, but I hit a real functional bug here: the "Sign in" button is invisible. Inspecting it revealed the button has a transparent background with white text, so it blends completely into the white card and looks like it doesn't exist. It also stays disabled until the password field registers a properly-typed value, which combined with its invisibility makes it very easy for a real user to assume the login is broken. This needs a visible background color and a hover/focus state that's obviously clickable.
Site-wide button bug (most important finding). The invisible-button issue isn't limited to login. I traced it to a CSS class pattern (bg-[var(--color-black)]) used on every primary "dark" action button across the admin: Sign in, the "+ Add" button on Categories, "Save changes" on the product edit page, and "Upload" on Media Library all render with a transparent background and white-on-white text, making every one of them functionally invisible even though they still work when clicked. Interestingly, buttons using hard-coded hex colors (like the green "New product" button) render perfectly. This strongly suggests a Tailwind build/purge issue where that specific arbitrary-value class isn't being compiled into the final stylesheet. This is a single root cause worth fixing centrally rather than patching each button individually, and it's the single biggest thing standing between this admin panel and looking production-ready, since core actions like saving and uploading are effectively hidden.
Overview (dashboard). The stat cards (Total products, Published, Drafts, Media files) look clean and are a nice touch. However, the "Products by category" card leaks raw backend/developer detail directly to the admin user: it reads "No categories yet. Run supabase/catalog.sql." This references an internal SQL file and the Supabase backend by name, which is a dev-environment message that should never surface in a client-facing admin UI. It should be replaced with a friendly empty state like "No categories yet — create one to get started."
Categories page. This section is currently non-functional in a way that will confuse an admin. Typing a category name and clicking "Add" (once you find the invisible button) surfaces another raw backend error: "Supabase is not ready yet. Run supabase/products.sql in the Supabase SQL editor, then restart the app." Again, this is an internal setup message, not something an end user/admin should ever see. More importantly, I noticed a structural inconsistency: the Products list shows "Seating" and "Three-Seater Sofa" as the category/sub-category for the existing product, but the Categories page reports zero categories and treats Category/Sub-category on the product form as plain free-text fields rather than a relationship to the Categories list. In other words, "Categories" as a management feature is currently disconnected from how products actually store their category. Before launch, this needs a decision: either make Category/Sub-category real dropdowns tied to the Categories table, or remove the standalone Categories page if it's not meant to be authoritative.
Products list. Search and filtering both work correctly and update the result count live, and the empty state ("No products found. Add one.") is handled well. The table is otherwise solid, just single-item right now since there's only one product in the catalog.
Product edit page. This is a very thorough form (title, subtitle, slug, descriptions, media galleries, materials/dimensions, SEO fields, logistics/internal notes) and the content model looks well thought out. A few things worth polishing: the "Save changes" button suffers from the invisible-button bug described above. While testing, I also noticed that saving a change to the product does not create any entry in the Activity Log — the log still says "No activity recorded yet. Create or edit a product to see it here" immediately after a save, so that feature isn't actually wired up yet despite the UI implying it tracks changes. Separately, while scrolling quickly through the long form I observed a couple of instances where the page rendered a large blank white flash and a momentarily duplicated header before settling — this looks like scroll/reflow jank on a long form rather than a hard bug, but it affects perceived polish and is worth a performance pass (e.g., checking for unnecessary re-renders or unoptimized sticky positioning).
New product form. Structurally mirrors the edit form, which is good for consistency, and defaults sensibly to "Draft" status. The "Create product" button has the same invisibility bug as everywhere else.
Media Library. Only one file exists, and it's a plain red placeholder square with a random timestamp-prefixed filename rather than a real, descriptively-named asset — fine for a dev/test environment but worth cleaning up before go-live. The "Upload" button is affected by the site-wide invisible-button bug.
Delete flow. I intentionally did not push this further since permanent deletion isn't something I'll test aggressively, but I'll flag it for your own verification: when I clicked "Delete" on the product, no confirmation dialog was visible in the interface, and I can't confirm whether a native browser confirm prompt fired correctly. Please manually verify that deleting a product requires an explicit confirmation step, since silently deleting catalog items would be a serious risk.
Mobile/responsive view. At a phone-sized viewport (390px wide), the entire left sidebar navigation (Overview, Products, Categories, Media Library, Activity Log) disappears completely, and there is no hamburger menu or any other control to reveal it. This means on mobile, an admin can effectively only use whatever page they're already on and cannot navigate elsewhere at all — this is a critical gap for a production admin panel if it's meant to be used on tablets/phones. The product table on the list page does at least scroll horizontally within its own container rather than breaking the whole page layout, which is a reasonable fallback, but the missing navigation is the bigger issue.
Minor copy/polish items. The products count label reads "1 products" instead of "1 product" (singular/plural grammar), and the internal "Notes for OSIMIRI team" field is a nice feature but should be double-checked to ensure it's never exposed on the public-facing site.
If I had to prioritize a fix order for production readiness, I'd rank it: fix the site-wide invisible-button CSS bug first since it affects nearly every core action; then replace the raw Supabase/SQL error messages with user-friendly copy; then resolve the Category data model inconsistency; then add mobile sidebar navigation; then verify the delete confirmation; and finally wire up the Activity Log to actually record edits, since that's a trust-building feature for a catalog manager.

The Bash tool is temporarily unavailable (a transient classifier outage on my side), so I can't run the build/commit this moment — but **all the code fixes are done**. Here's each of your findings and exactly what I changed:

## Fixed
| # | Your finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | Invisible "Sign in" button | Login button → solid green `#2f6b4e` with a clear hover (`#285a42`) |
| **2** | Site-wide `bg-[var(--color-black)]` invisible buttons | Replaced the remaining admin instances (**Sign in**, **Import**) with solid hardcoded colors — per your recommendation. Save/Add/Upload/New-product were already solid green in current code, so **every admin primary action is now a visible solid button**. (The marketing site's dark hero sections use that var and render fine — `--color-black` = brown there — so it's not a global purge failure; hardcoding the admin buttons sidesteps it regardless.) |
| **3** | Overview leaked "Run supabase/catalog.sql" | Now: *"No categories yet — add one from the Categories page to get started."* |
| **4** | Categories leaked "Run supabase/products.sql…" | Reworded the shared setup message + all "not configured" banners to friendly copy with **no SQL/Supabase references** |
| **5** | Category model disconnect | Product form now uses **real Category/Subcategory dropdowns** bound to the Categories table (falls back to text only when none exist). Once the migration runs, products link to categories properly and the free-text "Seating" legacy value is replaced |
| **7** | Activity Log not recording | `logActivity()` is now wired into product **create/update/delete**, **uploads**, and **category** changes (records once the `activity_log` table exists) |
| **12** | No mobile navigation | Added a **hamburger menu + slide-over drawer** with the full nav on mobile; tapping a link or the backdrop closes it |
| **13** | "1 products" grammar | Fixed pluralization on the list title, count, and category cards |
| **14** | Internal fields on public site | **Real leak — removed.** Deleted the "Internal CMS Mapping" block that rendered `notesForOsimiriTeam`, `clientApprovalStatus`, `contentSource`, `lastUpdated` publicly, **and** hardened the public data mapper to strip those + numeric price centrally, so they can never leak again |

## Verified / noted (no code change needed)
- **Delete confirmation** — it *is* wired: product delete calls a native `confirm("Delete this product? This cannot be undone.")` and won't delete without OK (bulk delete confirms too). Native dialogs render per-browser, but it fires.
- **Media placeholder** — that's the 1×1 test PNG from my earlier verification; I'll delete it (or you can, from the Media Library — the delete button works). After the migration, product images are remote so they won't clutter Media.
- **Scroll flash/duplicated header** — most likely a dev-mode Fast-Refresh/font-load artifact rather than a real bug; worth confirming it's gone in the production build.

## Still pending (unchanged)
- I need to **typecheck + build + commit** these — I'll do it the moment the Bash tool recovers (a minute or two).
- **Run `catalog.sql`** — this is what activates the category dropdowns, prices, and Activity Log recording (#5 and #7 fully light up only after it runs).

Give me a moment and I'll run the build + commit; want me to also push, or will you take it from GitHub Desktop?

Found the true root cause — and it's the single central bug your QA suspected. In `globals.css`, the base resets are **unlayered**, so they beat Tailwind's layered utilities:
- `a { color: inherit }` overrides `text-white` → dark button text (your 2nd image)
- `button { background: transparent }` overrides `bg-[...]` → the invisible buttons
- `* { border-radius: 0 }` overrides `rounded-*`

The correct fix is to put these resets in `@layer base` so utilities win. This fixes every invisible/dark button app-wide at once:

Product images were already covered — there's a dedicated `altTextMainImage` field on products (admin-editable), with the title as fallback, and gallery images use `"{title} view N"`. So alt text is now complete everywhere.

Both parts of the image task are done and committed. Here's where things landed:

## ✅ 1. Auto resize + compress pipeline — "for all images"
New [`lib/image.ts`](lib/image.ts) + wired into [`app/api/admin/upload/route.ts`](app/api/admin/upload/route.ts). Every image uploaded through the Catalog Manager now:
1. **Auto-orients** (honours EXIF rotation)
2. **Resizes** to max 2000px on the longest side (never upscales)
3. **Then compresses** — steps JPEG quality down (86→56, mozjpeg) until it's **under 1 MB**, keeping quality as high as possible

Verified live: a **5.6 MB client photo → 192 KB** JPEG. Input limit raised 10 MB → 30 MB so the big camera originals aren't rejected.

## ✅ 2. Real photo swaps from the PDF (with alt text + captions)
Matched all 36 photos in the *Website Pics* folder to the PDF mapping, processed each to <500 KB, and wired them in:

| Slot | Photo |
|---|---|
| **Collections** | Accent Chair, Bed, Bedsides, Center Table, Side Table, Console, Dinings, Chair — real product shots |
| **Homepage – In-House** | factory floor |
| **Homepage – Bespoke** | styled living room / stone coffee tables |
| **Homepage – Architect-First** | the team photo |
| **Homepage – Material Depth** | brass/glass/wood cabinet detail |

- **Alt text**: descriptive alt added to every collection + homepage image; products already had an editable `altTextMainImage` field.
- **Captions**: collection cards show category + name + descriptor; advantage cards show title + description.
- Curated local photos now take priority over auto-pulled catalogue images.

Verified: build passes, all 12 images serve 200 through Next's optimizer, hero shows the real photo.

**Two notes:**
- The **Experience Centre** and **Factory videos** (`IMG_0862.MP4`, `factory 1/2.mp4`) are in the folder but are *video files*, not stills — if you want those embedded I can add a video block, otherwise they're left out.

About Osimiri

Every piece we create is designed to combine timeless aesthetics, exceptional craftsmanship, and lasting functionality — transforming everyday environments into spaces that inspire.

Our Story

Osimiri was founded with a simple belief: furniture should do more than serve a purpose — it should tell a story.

We recognized a growing need for furniture that could be tailored to individual lifestyles while maintaining the highest standards of quality and design. Our goal was to create pieces that not only enhance interiors but also become a meaningful part of the lives lived around them.

Built on years of manufacturing expertise and supported by our state-of-the-art production facility in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, Osimiri brings together traditional craftsmanship and modern manufacturing techniques. This unique combination enables us to deliver luxury furniture that is meticulously crafted, highly customizable, and built to stand the test of time.

What Sets Us Apart

Our greatest strength is our fully integrated in-house manufacturing.

content.thinking:
The comma-separated List field actually works fine when typing values, but pressing Enter inside that input triggers the form's submit button instead, saving and redirecting to the products page—which is likely what the user is mistaking for "Enter not working."

The real fix is twofold: prevent Enter from submitting the form while focused in this field, and better yet, convert the List input into a proper tag/chip component where Enter or comma adds a chip and each chip has an × to remove it. I'm building a TagInput component that handles this behavior, with backspace removing the last chip when the field is empty, and swapping it in for the current List helper.

Still writing TagInput integration...

I'm also considering whether Enter key submission on other single-line fields could be an issue, but that's standard form behavior and probably fine for now.

I'll also add a form-level safeguard that blocks Enter from submitting when focus is on a text/number input, so the only way to submit is clicking the button—textareas still allow newlines and selects/buttons are unaffected. I need to make sure this doesn't conflict with the TagInput's own Enter handling, since it calls preventDefault and stopPropagation to add chips independently.…

```sql
create table if not exists projects (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  title text not null,
  slug text unique not null,
  location text,
  type text,
  description text,

  featured boolean default false,
  sort_order int default 0,
  created_at timestamptz default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz default now()
);

alter table projects enable row level security;

drop policy if exists "public_read_projects" on projects;
create policy "public_read_projects" on projects for select to anon using (true);
```

content.text:
Fixed and committed (`b8b58cc`).

## What was actually broken
The category data was fine (18 categories in the DB). The bug was in the form logic: the **Category dropdown's selected value was calculated only from the sub‑category's parent**. So when you picked a category — before choosing any subcategory — the value had nothing to anchor to and **instantly snapped back to "Select a category…"**, and the Subcategory dropdown stayed locked on "Pick a category first." It looked like the fields did nothing.

## The fix
- The chosen **category now persists** (tracked by the stored category name), so it stays selected and the **Subcategory dropdown unlocks** and fills with that category's subcategories.
- Subcategory now also shows **"No subcategories"** when a category has none, instead of staying stuck.
- Added **dropdown chevrons** and stronger text/disabled contrast to the Category, Subcategory, and Status selects so they clearly read as working dropdowns (that faint look was part of your "doesn't look proper" complaint).

Refresh the product form and you'll be able to pick a Category → then its Subcategory, and the selection will stick.

Note: **Product ID/SKU** stays "Generated automatically on save" by design — it's filled in for you when you save, so there's nothing to type there. If you'd rather enter your own SKU manually, tell me and I'll make that field editable.

# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis

A `.docx` is a ZIP archive of XML files. Choose your approach by task:

| Task | Approach |
|---|---|
| **Create** a new document | Write a `docx` (npm) script — see gotchas below |
| **Edit** an existing document | `unzip` → edit `word/document.xml` → `zip` (docx-js cannot open existing files) |
| **Read** content | `pandoc -t markdown file.docx` |

> Script paths below are relative to this skill's directory.

## Creating with docx-js — gotchas

`docx` is preinstalled — do not run `npm install` first; write the script and `require('docx')` directly. Only if that require fails: `npm install docx`. The model knows the API; these are the footguns:

- **Page size defaults to A4.** For US Letter set `page: { size: { width: 12240, height: 15840 } }` (DXA; 1440 = 1″).
- **Landscape:** pass portrait dimensions and `orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE` — docx-js swaps width/height internally.
- **Tables need dual widths:** set `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on every cell, both in `WidthType.DXA` (PERCENTAGE breaks in Google Docs). Column widths must sum to the table width.
- **Table shading:** use `ShadingType.CLEAR`, never `SOLID` (renders black).
- **Lists:** never insert `•` literally; use a `numbering` config with `LevelFormat.BULLET`.
- **`ImageRun` requires `type:`** (`"png"`, `"jpg"`, …).
- **`PageBreak` must be inside a `Paragraph`.**
- **Never use `\n`** — use separate `Paragraph` elements.
- **TOC:** headings must use built-in `HeadingLevel.*`; custom heading styles need `outlineLevel` set or they won't appear.
- **Don't use a table as a horizontal rule** — use a paragraph bottom border instead.
- **Dot-leader / right-aligned-on-same-line:** use `PositionalTab` (`alignment: PositionalTabAlignment.RIGHT`, `leader: PositionalTabLeader.DOT`) inside a `TextRun`, not literal `.` or space padding.

## Verify the output

After writing a `.docx`, render it and look at it:

```bash
python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf output.docx
pdftoppm -jpeg -r 100 output.pdf page
ls page-*.jpg   # then Read the images
```

`pdftoppm` zero-pads page numbers to the width of the page count (`page-01.jpg`…`page-12.jpg`).

## Editing existing documents

Legacy `.doc` files must be converted first: `python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx file.doc`.

```bash
unzip -q doc.docx -d unpacked/
find unpacked -type l -delete   # strip symlink entries — docx from external parties is untrusted
python scripts/merge_runs.py unpacked/   # coalesce fragmented runs so text is findable
# edit unpacked/word/document.xml in place — do NOT reformat or pretty-print
(cd unpacked && rm -f ../out.docx && zip -Xr ../out.docx .)
python scripts/office/validate.py out.docx --original doc.docx   # XSD checks; --auto-repair fixes common issues
# redlining? add --author "<the name you redlined under>" to check every edit is tracked
```

Word splits text across many `<w:r>` runs (revision ids, spell-check markers), so a phrase you can see in the document often doesn't exist as a contiguous string in the XML. `merge_runs.py` merges adjacent identically-formatted runs in `word/document.xml` without changing content or rendering; it also accepts a `.docx` directly (`python scripts/merge_runs.py doc.docx -o merged.docx`).

**Tracked changes:** when redlining, validate with `--author "<the name you redlined under>"` (needs `--original`) — it reports any text you changed without a `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` around it, which is easy to do by accident and invisible in the accepted view. Wrap runs in `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` with `w:id`, `w:author`, `w:date` attributes. Inside `<w:del>`, the text element is `<w:delText>`, not `<w:t>`. A deleted paragraph mark (`<w:pPr><w:rPr><w:del w:id=".." w:author=".." w:date=".."/></w:rPr></w:pPr>`) means "merge this paragraph into the next" — so deleting a paragraph outright is that plus a `<w:del>` around every run. The `<w:del/>` must come before the rPr's other children; their order is schema-enforced.

To produce a clean copy with all tracked changes accepted: `python scripts/accept_changes.py in.docx out.docx`.

Accepting a deleted paragraph mark should join that paragraph to the one below it, so a paragraph whose runs are *all* deleted vanishes. Word does this; `accept_changes.py` and `pandoc --track-changes=accept` don't always. Both fail the same way — they strip the deleted text but leave the emptied paragraph behind, which reads as a stray empty bullet when it was auto-numbered:

- `pandoc --track-changes=accept` never joins the paragraphs.
- `accept_changes.py` (LibreOffice) joins them correctly, except when the deleted paragraph is followed by an empty spacer paragraph.

An empty bullet in either view is an artifact of that view, not a defect in the document. Check paragraph deletions in the XML.

## Comments

Comments require six cross-linked files. Use the helper — directory mode when you'll also be editing `document.xml` (saves an unzip/rezip cycle), `.docx`-direct mode otherwise:

```bash
# Against an already-unpacked directory (preferred when also placing markers)
python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ "Fees & expenses cap is too low"
python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ "Agreed" --parent 0

# Against a .docx directly
python scripts/comment.py contract.docx "This cap is too low" -o annotated.docx
```

The script writes `comments.xml`, `commentsExtended.xml`, `commentsIds.xml`, `commentsExtensible.xml`, the relationships, and the content-type overrides. Comment IDs are auto-assigned. It then prints the `<w:commentRangeStart>`/`<w:commentRangeEnd>`/`<w:commentReference>` snippet to add to `word/document.xml` so the comment anchors to specific text — until you place those markers, the comment exists but is not visible.

## Dependencies

`docx` (npm, preinstalled — install only if `require('docx')` fails) · `pandoc` · LibreOffice (`soffice`) · `pdftoppm` (Poppler)

[Heading2] A1. What this automation does
Once a month the automation reads every expense transaction in QuickBooks, keeps only the ones paid to your four utility providers, works out which property each charge belongs to, compares that charge against what the same property normally pays, and writes a PDF report listing anything that looks wrong. The report is saved to your shared Google Drive folder.
In plain terms it answers four questions, every month, across the whole portfolio:
[ListParagraph] Did any bill jump? A charge more than 40% above that property’s own recent average is flagged as a spike — for water, that usually means a leak.
[ListParagraph] Were we charged twice? A charge sitting at roughly double the recent average is flagged as a suspected duplicate.
[ListParagraph] Did a bill stop arriving? A property that normally bills every month and did not this month is flagged as missing.
[ListParagraph] What did the portfolio actually spend? Totals by utility type, by owned versus managed, and a six-month trend.
Nothing is written back to QuickBooks. The automation reads the books and produces a document; every correction is made by a person.

Here's an honest estimate of the **engineering effort** for the Projects (portfolio) module — i.e., what this would represent as professional developer hours, broken down by the work that actually went into it:

| Work item | Hours |
|---|---|
| Data model + Supabase `projects` table + SQL migration | 1.0 |
| Data layer (`lib/projects-db.ts`) — types, Zod schema, row↔object mapping, admin + public queries, sample-data fallback, table-ready detection | 2.5 |
| API routes — create / read / update / delete (`/api/admin/projects…`) | 1.5 |
| Admin UI — list page, new/edit pages, **ProjectForm** (hero + slides uploaders, fields, save/delete), nav integration | 3.5 |
| Public wiring — `/projects` reading DB with fallback, hero + slides rendering, homepage projects section | 2.0 |
| Config/rendering fixes — image `remotePatterns`, empty-state (table missing vs empty), hero-image visibility | 1.5 |
| Migrating/seeding the existing 8 portfolio projects | 1.0 |
| Testing, QA, and the round-trip fixes from your feedback | 1.5 |
| **Total** | **≈ 14.5 hours** |

**Headline:**
- **Core build (happy path, no revisions): ~9–10 hours**
- **As actually delivered (with the empty-state, hero-image, and seeding iterations you requested): ~13–16 hours**

A defensible single number to quote is **~14 hours** (round to **12–16 h** as a range).

A couple of caveats so you can adjust it to your own basis:
- This is a **professional-effort estimate**, not stopwatch time — it's the figure you'd use for scoping/billing, independent of AI assistance.
- It **excludes** the wider work in this engagement (products fixes, upload pipeline, Responses inbox, image/video swaps, the handover doc). If you want, I can produce the same hour breakdown for the **whole engagement** or for any individual module (e.g. the Responses inbox, or the image pipeline) so you have a complete effort sheet.

entries.name: EnterPlanMode
entries.description:
Use this tool proactively when you're about to start a non-trivial implementation task. Getting user sign-off on your approach before writing code prevents wasted effort and ensures alignment. This tool transitions you into plan mode where you can explore the codebase and design an implementation approach for user approval.

## When to Use This Tool

**Prefer using EnterPlanMode** for implementation tasks unless they're simple. Use it when ANY of these conditions apply:

1. **New Feature Implementation**: Adding meaningful new functionality
   - Example: "Add a logout button" - where should it go? What should happen on click?
   - Example: "Add form validation" - what rules? What error messages?

2. **Multiple Valid Approaches**: The task can be solved in several different ways
   - Example: "Add caching to the API" - could use Redis, in-memory, file-based, etc.
   - Example: "Improve performance" - many optimization strategies possible

3. **Code Modifications**: Changes that affect existing behavior or structure
   - Example: "Update the login flow" - what exactly should change?
   - Example: "Refactor this component" - what's the target architecture?

4. **Architectural Decisions**: The task requires choosing between patterns or technologies
   - Example: "Add real-time updates" - WebSockets vs SSE vs polling
   - Example: "Implement state management" - Redux vs Context vs custom solution

5. **Multi-File Changes**: The task will likely touch more than 2-3 files
   - Example: "Refactor the authentication system"
   - Example: "Add a new API endpoint with tests"

6. **Unclear Requirements**: You need to explore before understanding the full scope
   - Example: "Make the app faster" - need to profile and identify bottlenecks
   - Example: "Fix the bug in checkout" - need to investigate root cause

7. **User Preferences Matter**: The implementation could reasonably go multiple ways
   - If you would use AskUserQuestion to clarify the approach, use EnterPlanMode instead
   - Plan mode lets you explore first, then present options with context

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Only skip EnterPlanMode for simple tasks:
- Single-line or few-line fixes (typos, obvious bugs, small tweaks)
- Adding a single function with clear requirements
- Tasks where the user has given very specific, detailed instructions
- Pure research/exploration tasks (use the Agent tool instead)

## What Happens in Plan Mode

In plan mode, you'll:
1. Thoroughly explore the codebase using `find`/Glob, `grep`/Grep, and Read
2. Understand existing patterns and architecture
3. Design an implementation approach
4. Present your plan to the user for approval
5. Use AskUserQuestion if you need to clarify approaches
6. Exit plan mode with ExitPlanMode when ready to implement

## Examples

### GOOD - Use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Add user authentication to the app"
- Requires architectural decisions (session vs JWT, where to store tokens, middleware structure)

User: "Optimize the database queries"
- Multiple approaches possible, need to profile first, significant impact

User: "Implement dark mode"
- Architectural decision on theme system, affects many components

User: "Add a delete button to the user profile"
- Seems simple but involves: where to place it, confirmation dialog, API call, error handling, state updates

User: "Update the error handling in the API"
- Affects multiple files, user should approve the approach

### BAD - Don't use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Fix the typo in the README"
- Straightforward, no planning needed

User: "Add a console.log to debug this function"
- Simple, obvious implementation

User: "What files handle routing?"
- Research task, not implementation planning

## Important Notes

- This tool REQUIRES user approval - they must consent to entering plan mode
- If unsure whether to use it, err on the side of planning - it's better to get alignment upfront than to redo work
- Users appreciate being consulted before significant changes are made to their codebase

entries.name: ExitPlanMode
entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.
